items.stem: A formula references Table1[Amount]. A user adds 50 new rows to the table. What happens to the formula result?

options.text: It automatically includes the new rows because the structured reference expands
options.rationale: Correct: structured references expand and contract with the table.

options.text: It keeps the original row count and ignores new rows
options.rationale: Structured references are not fixed to the original size.

options.text: It returns an error until the formula is edited
options.rationale: No edit is required; the reference adjusts automatically.

options.text: It only updates after the workbook is reopened
options.rationale: The reference updates on recalculation, not on reopen.

items.explanation: Correct: structured references expand and contract with the table.
items.provenance: original Mastemy item drafted by an AI agent; no external question source

items.stem: Which TWO are true about Excel data validation? (Select TWO.)

options.text: A list rule can present an in-cell dropdown of allowed values
options.rationale: Correct: list validation can show an in-cell dropdown.

options.text: A custom rule can use a formula that returns TRUE for valid entries
options.rationale: Correct: custom validation evaluates a formula per entry.

options.text: Validation always blocks a plain paste of an invalid value
options.rationale: A plain paste can bypass validation; it is not always triggered.

options.text: Validation permanently locks the cell against any future edits
options.rationale: Validation constrains entries; it does not lock the cell.

items.explanation: Correct: list validation can show an in-cell dropdown.

items.stem: Why separate inputs, calculations and outputs onto distinct areas of a workbook?

options.text: So assumptions can be changed in one place without hunting through formulas
options.rationale: Correct: isolating inputs makes a model easier to update and audit.

options.text: Because Excel refuses to calculate across sheets otherwise
options.rationale: Excel calculates across sheets fine; this is a design choice.

options.text: To reduce the file size of the workbook
options.rationale: Layering does not meaningfully change file size.

options.text: Because named ranges only work on separate sheets
options.rationale: Named ranges work regardless of layering.

items.explanation: Correct: isolating inputs makes a model easier to update and audit.
